_comment: Edit this file to point the skill at a different scope, cadence, or delivery target. Nothing in the skill or workflow files should need to change for a new deployment - if it does, that's a bug in the skill, not a config gap.

scope._note: When mode is 'regions', include_regions holds country names, region names, or IATA/ICAO codes and discovery is restricted to them. Empty include_regions with mode 'global' means no restriction. exclude_regions applies in either mode.

cadence._note: flash_pass_minutes is 60, not the originally-planned 15-20 - that's a real platform floor discovered while building Batch 1, not a preference. The durable Routine/trigger mechanism (the only scheduling primitive that survives past this session and doesn't expire) has a hard minimum interval of 1 hour. A sub-hourly primitive exists (CronCreate) but is session-scoped, auto-expires after 7 days, and only fires while the session's REPL is idle - not viable for standing production monitoring. Both passes are implemented as separate Routines: .claude/workflows/airport-disruption-flash-pass.js (fewer buckets, runs every flash_pass_minutes) and .claude/workflows/airport-disruption-deep-pass.js (all buckets, runs every deep_pass_hours).

dashboard._note: auto_refresh means the dashboard is regenerated and republished as the last step of every successful cycle, once that step exists (build-plan Batch 4). There is no in-page 'run now' control - a published Artifact cannot trigger a skill run; see the operating plan, section 9.

email._note: Disabled until a Gmail/Outlook connector is authorized on this org and the digest formatter (build-plan Batch 5) exists. digest_style is a hint to the digest-rendering step to include a supply-chain-relevant visual, not a raw text dump.

feature_flags._note: flight_tracking_api requires an actual provider account and API key (build-plan Batch 3) before it can be turned on. verification_pass gates the thin-sourced/high-impact re-check step (build-plan Batch 2).

budgets._note: max_tokens_per_cycle_hint is informational context for whoever is sizing cadence/scope, not an enforced runtime cap - the workflow script has no way to abort mid-run on token spend today. Per-agent timeouts are similarly a soft bound, not a hard one: the Agent tool exposes no timeout parameter, so both workflow scripts instruct discovery agents to move on after two failed attempts at a source rather than actually killing a stuck call.

reliability._note: A coverage gap is declared when the most recent success in ops_log_path for a given pass_type is older than coverage_gap_threshold_cycles times that pass's own cadence (2 hours for flash, 10 hours for deep, at current cadence). pending_classification_path holds raw candidates from a deep-pass cycle whose classify step failed, to be replayed via args.pendingCandidates on the next deep-pass run rather than discarded; the flash pass does not bother checkpointing - its own next cycle is at most an hour away.
